title: The effect of ChatGPT on students’ learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking: insights from a meta-analysis
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether ChatGPT improves student learning and under what conditions its effects are strongest. It addresses three outcomes: learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking, responding to mixed findings in the prior literature about whether ChatGPT helps, has no effect, or may even hinder learning.

The authors conducted a meta-analysis of 51 quasi-experimental and experimental studies published between November 2022 and February 2025, extracting 72 independent effect sizes. The included studies covered primary, secondary, and college learners, though the quantitative moderator analyses were mainly driven by secondary and college samples. The contexts included STEM and related courses, language learning and academic writing, and skills/competencies development; learning models included personalized learning, problem-based learning, project-based learning, contextual learning, reflective learning, and mixed designs. ChatGPT was used in roles such as intelligent tutor, intelligent partner, intelligent learning tool, and mixed roles, and in applications such as assessment/evaluation, tutoring, and personalized recommendation.

The meta-analysis found a large positive effect of ChatGPT on learning performance, and moderate positive effects on learning perception and higher-order thinking. For learning performance, effects were stronger in skills/competencies courses, problem-based learning, and 4–8 week interventions. For learning perception, duration was the only significant moderator, with longer interventions producing larger effects. For higher-order thinking, effects varied by course type and were strongest when ChatGPT functioned as an intelligent tutor. Overall, the paper concludes that ChatGPT can support learning outcomes, but its effectiveness depends on instructional design, duration, and how it is integrated into teaching and learning.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis of 51 experimental/quasi-experimental studies with standardized effect sizes, heterogeneity tests, publication-bias checks, and sensitivity analyses. The design is strong for causal synthesis, though there is substantial heterogeneity across included studies.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effects are medium-to-large and positive for the main outcomes, especially learning performance (g=0.867) and moderate effects for learning perception and higher-order thinking (g≈0.46). This indicates meaningful impact on general student learning outcomes, although the evidence spans mixed contexts rather than middle school mathematics specifically.

interventions.use_case: Meta-analysis of ChatGPT used as an intelligent tutor, learning partner, or educational tool in experimental and quasi-experimental learning interventions across K-12 and college settings.

finding.finding_summary: Across 44 independent studies, ChatGPT had a large positive effect on learning performance (Hedges's g=0.867, 95% CI 0.683 to 1.052). Outcomes were measured with post-test scores, exams, and comparable achievement assessments in experimental and quasi-experimental studies (total studies in the overall meta-analysis: 51; performance subset k=44).

ChatGPT had a moderate positive effect on learning perception across 19 independent studies (g=0.456, 95% CI 0.287 to 0.625). The paper reports this construct as learner perceptions measured primarily through scales and questionnaires, indicating improved attitudes/experience with ChatGPT-supported learning.

ChatGPT had a moderate positive effect on higher-order thinking across 9 independent studies (g=0.457, 95% CI 0.255 to 0.650). The included studies measured higher-order thinking with scales/questionnaires, capturing outcomes such as critical thinking and related cognitive processes.
